summary: community.vmware breaking changes: it depends on vmware.vmware and the vmware-vcenter/vapi client packages, requires pyVmomi 8.0.3.0.1+ and ansible-core 2.17+, removes run_command_in_guest and the security_override options of vmware_dvs_portgroup(_info), and drops vm_tools_install_status.
questions: What pyVmomi version does community.vmware require now?
Which collection does community.vmware depend on?
Why is security_override rejected by vmware_dvs_portgroup?
What ansible-core version is needed for community.vmware in Ansible 11?

answer_card.title: community.vmware breaking changes in Ansible 11
answer_card.answer_md:
- Requires ansible-core 2.17+ and pyVmomi 8.0.3.0.1+.
- Depends on the `vmware.vmware` collection and the `vmware-vcenter` / `vmware-vapi-common-client` packages.
- `vmware_dvs_portgroup`: the `security_override` alias is removed. Use `mac_management_override`. `vmware_dvs_portgroup_info` no longer returns `security_override`.
- `vmware_guest_tools_info` no longer returns `vm_tools_install_status`.
- `run_command_in_guest()` is removed from module utils.
